title: The Unsinkable Ghost Ship That Lost 25 People

basis.note: not enough measured videos yet; using fixed default

segments.narration: On November 10, 1955, a merchant ship found the Joyita drifting six hundred miles off course in the South Pacific.
The ship was flooded, but structurally unsinkable. Yet all twenty-five passengers and crew were gone.
On deck lay bloody bandages, and a radio tuned to distress with its antenna snapped. Who cuts their own lifeline?
Every clock on board was frozen at 10:25, and the ship's log was completely stripped away.
They abandoned a vessel that could not sink, stepping into the dark ocean to disappear forever.

verdicts.claim: The MV Joyita was discovered abandoned in the South Pacific in November 1955.
verdicts.note: The vessel was sighted abandoned on November 10, 1955, north of Vanua Levu in the South Pacific.

verdicts.claim: There were 25 passengers and crew members missing from the MV Joyita.
verdicts.note: The article confirms 25 people (16 crew members and 9 passengers) disappeared from the ship.

verdicts.claim: The emergency radio aboard the Joyita was tuned to the international distress frequency.
verdicts.note: The radio was found tuned to 2182 kHz, the international marine radiotelephone distress channel.

verdicts.claim: Clocks found aboard the MV Joyita had stopped at 10:25.
verdicts.note: The electric clocks aboard the ship had stopped at 10:25.
